gates.text: Run [autopilot-full](#autopilot-full) without merging. Inherit its ownership, artifact proof, review, CI, custody, countersign and stop gates. Choose this route when the operator lands the PRs, whether the work is independent or dependent. Where this route differs, it wins: there is no merge or merge prep, and a dependent PR's code-ready and fix-round rebases target its actual parent instead of trunk.

1. Stop at verified and green on each current head, report merge-ready and hand the PRs to the operator. Do not merge or arm auto-merge. After handoff nobody pushes without the operator's go. Every audit or authorized loop tick names this route and its no-merge rule. Re-read both routes at each audit and refresh finished-owner records from actual state.

2. Stack a PR only when it builds on another PR. Independent PRs branch from trunk. A dependent PR targets its actual parent's branch; the root targets trunk. Each PR's sole owner performs its separately authorized own-branch rebase onto that parent (or trunk for a root), with the exact-head lease and custody rules from autopilot-full. The coordinator sequences dependencies but never becomes a second branch writer.

3. A lower PR's new head requires its dependent PR owners to restack above it in order. Compare each patch against its actual parent. An unchanged git patch-id may carry a verdict under [shipping](#shipping)'s evidence rule; changed material needs the appropriate new-head verification, and every new head needs its own green CI. Do not use the carry rule to waive repository or user review requirements.

4. Hand off each PR's base, dependency if any, exact head, verdict, CI evidence and owner. There is no forced linear stack or root-only writer. Freeze further pushes at handoff until operator go; any later landing follows separately authorized [shipping](#shipping), not this no-merge route.
**Reply.** Each PR and verdict, exact head/base, real dependencies, frozen handoff custody, remaining operator gates and parked follow-ups. Report no merges as this route's work.
